A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photon spectra are enhanced in the presence of magnetic field and anisotropy in general.
the magnetic field can enhance the photon spectra at high frequencies, while the pressure anisotropies will suppress the photon spectra in general.

the anisotropy and magnetic field can be utilized to tune the photon spectra, and the anisotropies can be generated by different methods, such as the collisional effects, the magnetic field or even the quark mass.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the anisotropic effect on photon production is significant in the presence of magnetic field and it is crucial to take the anisotropy into account when we try to understand the experimental data from RHIC and LHC.
the anisotropic effects on the photon production can be significant in the strongly coupled plasma, which can be tested by the future heavy ion collision experiments.
